meaning: を · object marker ("does X to Y")
gist: [本|ほん]を[読|よ]みます。 を marks the direct object — the thing the verb acts on. Say を as お. Pattern: Object + を + verb-ます. Do not use が for this object role, and do not put を after the verb.

rows: コーヒーを[飲|の]みます。
[私|わたし]は[手紙|てがみ]を[書|か]きます。
formation.note: を comes right after the object noun. Pronounce を as お. Topic は / も can still frame the sentence: [私|わたし]は本を読みます / [田中|たなか]さんもコーヒーを飲みます.

explanation: When a verb acts on something, mark that something with を: [本|ほん]を[読|よ]みます (read a book), コーヒーを[飲|の]みます (drink coffee), [映画|えいが]を[見|み]ます (watch a movie). The particle is written を but pronounced お. Keep the order Object + を + verb — never ×[行|い]きますを. For the thing being read, watched, or drunk, use を, not が: ×[本|ほん]が[読|よ]みます is wrong for "(I) read a book."

senses.label: Object of an action
senses.body: を marks what the verb acts on: books, coffee, movies, music.
senses.example_en: I read a book. / I read books.

senses.label: Food and drink
senses.body: Things you eat or drink take を before the verb.
senses.example_ruby: コーヒーを[飲|の]みます。

senses.label: Media and speech
senses.body: Movies, music, letters, and languages also take を.
senses.example_en: I watch a movie. / I watch movies.

senses.label: Topic + object
senses.body: は / も can mark the topic while を still marks the object.
senses.example_ruby: [私|わたし]は[手紙|てがみ]を[書|か]きます。
senses.example_en: I write a letter. / I write letters.

register_context: Polite classroom speech: Objectを + verb-ます. Pronounce を as お even though the kana is を. Keep topics with は / も when useful; the object still needs を.

mistakes.why: The thing you read is the object → を, not が. (が marks a subject of existence or focus, not this object role.)
を attaches to the object noun before the verb — never after the verb.
を comes after the object: 本を読みます.

mistakes.wrong_ruby: コーヒーは[飲|の]みます。(Meaning: stating what you drink as the object, not contrasting topics)
mistakes.right_ruby: コーヒーを[飲|の]みます。
mistakes.why: For a plain object reading, use を. は on the object is contrast/topic, not the basic pattern.

contrasts.label: Bare verb vs object + を
contrasts.summary: [読|よ]みます names the action. [本|ほん]を[読|よ]みます names what you read.

contrasts.label: が (subject) vs を (object)
contrasts.summary: が marks who/what exists or is focused as subject. を marks the thing acted on.

contrasts.label: Pronunciation: を = お
contrasts.summary: Written を, spoken お — same particle either way.
contrasts.ex_a_en: (Say: ほんをよみます → ほんおよみます)
contrasts.ex_b_ruby: コーヒーを[飲|の]みます。
contrasts.ex_b_en: (Say: コーヒーをのみます → コーヒーおのみます)

examples.english: I read a book. / I read books.

examples.ruby: コーヒーを[飲|の]みます。
[音楽|おんがく]を[聞|き]きます。
[日本語|にほんご]を[話|はな]します。
[新聞|しんぶん]を[買|か]います。
[私|わたし]は[本|ほん]を[読|よ]みます。

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.english: What will you read? / What do you read?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ruby: [本|ほん]を[読|よ]みます。[新聞|しんぶん]も[読|よ]みます。
dialogue.english: I read books. I read the newspaper too.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ruby: [音楽|おんがく]を[聞|き]きますか。

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ruby: はい、[音楽|おんがく]を[聞|き]ます。コーヒーも[飲|の]みます。
dialogue.english: Yes, I listen to music. I drink coffee too.

checks.why: Object of reading takes を: 本を読みます.
Object of drinking takes を: コーヒーを飲みます.

checks.prompt: How do you pronounce を in 本を読みます?

checks.why: Object + を + verb. ×映画が見ます uses the wrong particle; ×見ますを映画 puts を in the wrong place.
Language as object of 話す takes を.
